benchmark_points.bp1: Gammon India Limited's bank facilities have been in NPA status since June 2017.

benchmark_points.bp30: Loans to related parties constitute about 98.6% of loans given and are largely provided for.

benchmark_points.bp46: Corporate guarantees given to bankers total ₹746.35 cr.
benchmark_points.bp47: Several SPVs and Dutch holding companies have large negative net worth, un-audited accounts, or qualified accounts at Ansaldo Caldaie.
benchmark_points.bp48: Standalone turnover for FY2025-26 is ₹85.18 cr against a net loss after tax of ₹(1,189.01) cr.
benchmark_points.bp49: Consolidated net loss after tax for FY2025-26 is ₹(1,170.34) cr.

benchmark_points.bp52: Standalone accumulated losses stand at ₹(13,760.87) cr.

agent_points.ap1: The credit-risk situation at Gammon India Limited (GIL) is critical and distressed, characterized by comprehensive debt recalls, ongoing lender NPA classifications since June 2017, multiple winding-up petitions from unpaid stakeholders, soaring financial losses, and persistent going-concern warnings from statutory auditors.
agent_points.ap2: For the financial year ended March 31, 2026, the Group posted a net loss after tax of ₹1,170.34 crores compared to ₹1,192.34 crores in the previous year.
agent_points.ap3: The net loss for FY 2025-26 was driven heavily by high finance costs of ₹1,123.06 crores and massive impairments on legacy domestic and international exposures.
agent_points.ap4: Total credit facilities recalled by lenders stand at ₹3,923.59 crores alongside overdrawn credit facilities of ₹1,417.31 crores.
agent_points.ap5: Secured lenders have marked all credit facilities of the Company as Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) continuously since June 2017.
agent_points.ap6: Due to defaults, lenders have recalled the entire credit portfolio, reclassifying all long-term and short-term debt under current financial liabilities.
agent_points.ap7: Recalled Long-Term Term Loans and NCDs stand at ₹2,636.59 crores on a Standalone basis and ₹3,923.59 crores at the Group level as of March 31, 2026, up from ₹3,803.90 crores in FY2025.
agent_points.ap8: Overdrawn and short-term facilities recalled stand at ₹1,417.31 crores compared to ₹1,352.77 crores in FY2025.
agent_points.ap9: Cumulative interest accrued and booked on NPAs reached ₹3,786.28 crores as of March 31, 2026, compared to ₹3,105.83 crores as of March 31, 2025.
agent_points.ap10: The severe liquidity crunch has triggered multiple winding-up petitions filed against the Company by various stakeholders seeking debt recovery, which management reports are being settled according to mutually agreed repayment terms.
agent_points.ap11: IDBI Bank invoked 93,000,000 shares of AJR Infra & Tolling Limited held by Gammon Power Limited.
agent_points.ap12: IDBI Bank Dubai invoked the Standby Letter of Credit issued by IDBI Mumbai in October 2016 for overseas subsidiary Campo Puma Oriente S.A., with a total unprovided/provided exposure of ₹430.19 crores.
agent_points.ap13: Independent statutory auditors issued a material uncertainty related to going concern paragraph in both the Standalone and Consolidated Audit Reports.
agent_points.ap14: Statutory auditors and CARO reports flagged multiple adverse or qualified remarks regarding Gammon India Limited and subsidiaries under clauses governing fixed asset records, inventory/receivables, statutory dues, and internal controls.
agent_points.ap15: Auditors questioned the carrying value of ongoing/completed/terminated contract claims retained at ₹10.00 crore by the Company as of March 31, 2026, though management defended this via independent techno-legal validation.
agent_points.ap16: Gammon's exposure to Sofinter S.p.A. (Italy) has been written down/provided for on a prudence basis, with Gammon's share subject to dilution from 10% to 8.33% if it opts out of capital increase payments valued at roughly €66 million total by a third party.
agent_points.ap17: Campo Puma Oriente S.A. is characterized by partner disputes, oil field losses, and an invoked SBLC, with its entire exposure of ₹430.19 crores fully provided for.
agent_points.ap18: Sadelmi S.p.A. and Busi Power S.r.l. in Italy enforced creditors' protection through Italian courts due to severe contract issues, with court decisions delayed due to creditor objections.
agent_points.ap19: Gactel Turnkeys Projects Limited is subject to Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) via NCLT Mumbai branch order dated March 27, 2024, resulting in a total write-off of the company's exposure.

per_question.query: We still carry legacy exposure to Gammon India. Pull together every credit-risk event and red flag in this year's report - lender actions, payment defaults, auditor concerns, market and governance fallout - and tell me how serious the situation really is.

benchmark_points.bp1: Gammon India's revival story rests on a lender-approved resolution plan and a proposed one-time settlement (OTS) backed by a new investor.
benchmark_points.bp2: The auditor's report, balance sheet, and history of stalled approvals do not support management's optimism regarding Gammon India's revival.
benchmark_points.bp3: Settlement sources are mostly contingent, including unrealised arbitration awards, a Gammon House property under enforcement, pledged shares, and a potential sale of the Sofinter stake.
benchmark_points.bp4: No firm, committed cash source is identified in the Gammon India report excerpts.
benchmark_points.bp5: A Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR) referral for Gammon India occurred in March 2013.
benchmark_points.bp6: A CDR package was approved in June 2013 and a Master Restructuring Agreement was signed in September 2013.
benchmark_points.bp7: A Strategic Debt Restructuring (SDR) took place under which lenders received about 62% equity.
benchmark_points.bp8: An Inter-Creditor Agreement (ICA) was executed in 2019 under the RBI's 7 June 2019 circular.
benchmark_points.bp9: The core mechanism of the resolution plan involved hiving off the main business, which resolved 75% of lender dues.
benchmark_points.bp10: The residual company's primary task is to maximize recovery to repay residual debt.
benchmark_points.bp11: An OTS proposal was submitted at the lenders' request and is under consideration.
benchmark_points.bp12: Management describes the OTS as subject to waiver of interest and penal charges and a haircut on the principal outstanding.
benchmark_points.bp13: Gammon India's revival is conditional on an investor infusing further funds.
benchmark_points.bp14: In FY2012-13, Gammon India experienced a slowdown, project delays, stretched working capital, and referral to CDR.
benchmark_points.bp15: In November 2015, a scheme of corporate realignment and SDR were approved.
benchmark_points.bp16: In June 2017, facilities were classified as Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) and lenders recalled loans.
benchmark_points.bp17: In 2019, Deloitte was appointed as Process Advisor and Duff & Phelps was engaged for valuation.
benchmark_points.bp18: Post-2019, seven lenders gave in-principle sanction to a draft plan, but the Everstone investor fund closed due to delay by other bankers.
benchmark_points.bp19: In 2022, an alternate investor on the same terms was accepted by bankers, but a Joint Lenders' Meeting on 5 March 2022 disagreed on the timeline, leaving the plan unconcluded.
benchmark_points.bp20: Between 2023 and 2024, debt was assigned to Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs), specifically Union Bank to OARPL in 2024, and IDBI, Canara, and PNB to CFM.
benchmark_points.bp21: In FY2025-26, more than 50% of Gammon India's debt was assigned to ARCs, and the company was negotiating waivers and haircuts with them.
benchmark_points.bp22: The Report states that a repeated partial approved resolution process is not serving the purpose.
benchmark_points.bp23: CFM ARC has considered settling on principal only while waiving interest and penalties, though approval is pending.
benchmark_points.bp24: Management reports positive discussions with ARCs.
benchmark_points.bp25: The auditor states that the plan is dependent on too many variables and there is no progress.
benchmark_points.bp26: The auditor reports that lenders are not able to reach a consensus, with hardly any progress.
benchmark_points.bp27: Trading in Gammon India equity shares is suspended, and several creditors have filed winding-up petitions.
benchmark_points.bp28: Current liabilities exceed current assets by Rs 12,701.41 crore as of 31 March 2026.
benchmark_points.bp29: The company has severe manpower issues and is defaulting on statutory obligations.
benchmark_points.bp30: Gammon India's holding company is referred to NCLT and is unable to extend any kind of financial support.
benchmark_points.bp31: Management states that cash flows from projects could not be materialised.
benchmark_points.bp32: As of 31 March 2026, total standalone current assets are Rs 20.61 crore, cash is Rs 0.00 crore, and bank balances are Rs 2.82 crore with some restricted.
benchmark_points.bp33: Net cash from operations in FY2025-26 was Rs 6.55 crore.
benchmark_points.bp34: The auditor notes cash losses of Rs 1,048.68 crore in the current year.
benchmark_points.bp35: Non-current trade receivables are Rs 541.52 crore, mostly disputed awards under appeal by clients.
benchmark_points.bp36: Recoverability of Rs 532.91 crore depends on the outcome of appeals, and realisation continues to remain a big challenge.
benchmark_points.bp37: The Chennai Metro Rail Limited (CMRL) award was reduced to Rs 408 crore.
benchmark_points.bp38: Banks have taken over possession of Gammon House under SARFAESI, and the company is restrained from parting with rights.
benchmark_points.bp39: Gammon House is subject to first and second charges in favour of lenders.
benchmark_points.bp40: Net block of fixed assets is Rs 401.57 crore, of which freehold property is Rs 393.14 crore.
benchmark_points.bp41: Investments in impaired subsidiaries amounting to Rs 1,536.59 crore are fully provided for.
benchmark_points.bp42: Loans to related parties of Rs 2,978.81 crore are provided as doubtful.
benchmark_points.bp43: A new investor would acquire a 90% stake in Sofinter for Euro 12 million.
benchmark_points.bp44: The Gammon group's maximum exit from Sofinter is Euro 34 million at a Euro 135 million exit value.
benchmark_points.bp45: The Gammon group needs about Euro 14 million of fresh equity for Sofinter, with a shortfall undertaking from Nova Energy.
benchmark_points.bp46: The Sofinter stake is fully provided for on a prudent basis.
benchmark_points.bp47: Shares of subsidiaries and associates totaling 13,89,63,414 shares are pledged with lenders.
benchmark_points.bp48: The IDBI invocation of AJR Infra shares reversed a provision of Rs 6.51 crore.
benchmark_points.bp49: Gammon India retained good claims of only Rs 10.00 crore.
benchmark_points.bp50: Overdue principal stands at Rs 4,053.90 crore and interest default stands at Rs 2,820.26 crore.
benchmark_points.bp51: Penal interest of Rs 911.54 crore, including Rs 519.78 crore from CFM ARC, is contingent and not provided for.
benchmark_points.bp52: Right of recompense to CDR lenders of Rs 504.96 crore is disclosed as a contingent liability.
benchmark_points.bp53: The excerpts do not give the OTS amount, the haircut percentage, or the investor's identity and commitment size.
benchmark_points.bp54: The excerpts do not show lenders' approval status or an agreed settlement quantum.
benchmark_points.bp55: Campo Puma Oriente exposure is stated as Rs 430.19 crore with full provision, but elsewhere a provision of Rs 230.41 crore is disclosed.
benchmark_points.bp56: The Kaleshwaram project with a balance of Rs 681 crore and the Kolkata Metro package with a balance of Rs 9.49 crore are listed as ongoing contracts without details on cash contribution to a settlement.

agent_points.ap1: Gammon India's revival story faces severe material uncertainties and lacks a finalized resolution plan.
agent_points.ap2: The resolution framework is built upon negotiations with lenders and Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) for principal haircuts, the waiver of interest and penal charges, and the introduction of a new or alternate investor.
agent_points.ap3: Over the years, the plan has evolved through Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR), Strategic Debt Restructuring (SDR) in November 2015, an Inter-creditor Agreement (ICA) executed in 2019 under the RBI circular of June 7, 2019, various proposed investor iterations up to March 2022, and subsequent debt assignments to ARCs.
agent_points.ap4: Key physical assets—specifically the Gammon House property and its appurtenant land—have been seized by ARCs (Omkara Assets Reconstruction Private Limited and CFM Asset Reconstruction Company) under the SARFAESI Act, 2002.
agent_points.ap5: Current liabilities exceed current assets by Rs. 12,701.41 Crores as of March 31, 2026.
agent_points.ap6: The draft resolution plan involves restructuring, change in ownership, a potential investor bringing in further funds, and negotiations for a haircut on outstanding principal alongside the total waiver of interest and penal charges.
agent_points.ap7: Aggregate penal interest and charges considered contingent and not accounted for by the company—inclusive of possible settlement amounts—total Rs. 911.54 Crores.
agent_points.ap8: Aggregate penal interest and charges include Rs. 519.78 Crores specifically levied by CFM Assets Reconstruction Company Private Limited.
agent_points.ap9: Pursuant to recommendations by Deloitte, the company engaged Duff & Phelps (D&P) to evaluate the company and estimate the recoverability of its arbitration claims.
agent_points.ap10: Post-2013, the company posted major financial losses for the first time in nearly 80 years due to economic recession and shifting policies, following its inability to repay lenders, and was admitted to Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR).
agent_points.ap11: In November 2015, lenders approved a scheme of corporate realignment and Strategic Debt Restructuring (SDR), converting a portion of debt into equity and giving lenders a ~62% stake in GIL.
agent_points.ap12: On June 7, 2019, lenders executed an Inter-creditor Agreement (ICA) pursuant to the RBI Circular dated June 7, 2019, followed by submission of a draft resolution plan.
agent_points.ap13: In 2021, a resolution plan was approved by some lenders, though remaining under discussion and lacking full consensus.
agent_points.ap14: On March 5, 2022, due to time constraints, Gammon proposed an alternate investor on the same terms, but during a Joint Lenders Meeting, top management of certain lenders disagreed on timelines, leaving the resolution plan unconcluded.
agent_points.ap15: Between 2024 and 2026, more than 50% of the debt was assigned by lenders to Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs), alongside security assignments and enforcement notices.
agent_points.ap16: More than 50% of the debt has been assigned to two ARCs: Omkara Assets Reconstruction Private Limited and CFM Asset Reconstruction Company.
agent_points.ap17: ARCs have issued notices under the SARFAESI Act, 2002, taking over possession of the Gammon House property, including appurtenant land, and restraining the company from parting with rights over it.
agent_points.ap18: Lenders have recalled all loans and facilities.
agent_points.ap19: Equity share trading is suspended, creditors have filed winding-up petitions, bankers have placed embargoes on company assets, and the company suffers from severe manpower constraints alongside statutory and regulatory defaults.
agent_points.ap20: Overseas subsidiaries such as Gammon Europe S.p.A. and Gammon Holding BV report fully eroded net worth and net current liabilities of Euro 2.89 Crores (Rs. 315.46 Crores) and Euro 2.50 Crores (Rs. 272.85 Crores), respectively.

per_question.query: Suppose an asset reconstruction company asks whether Gammon India's revival story is credible. What is the resolution plan built on, how has it evolved over the years, and what assets or cash sources actually stand behind any settlement?

benchmark_points.bp1: The excerpts give little basis for relying on the Company's compliance, oversight or internal controls as currently described.
benchmark_points.bp2: The directors' statements regarding compliance and controls are mostly generic or procedural.
benchmark_points.bp3: The statutory auditor, the secretarial auditor Pramod Shah & Associates, and the practising company secretary certifying governance all report material failures.
benchmark_points.bp4: Several of the directors' own statements are contradicted by the same report.
benchmark_points.bp5: The Board composition and some procedural points are corroborated, but the substantive picture is weak.
benchmark_points.bp6: Directors state that internal controls are designed to give assurance on reliable reporting, statutory compliance and safeguarding of assets, but implementation and effectiveness in certain areas are affected due to manpower and liquidity issues [AR p.33].
benchmark_points.bp7: The statutory auditor cannot state that internal financial controls were adequate or operating effectively as at 31 March 2026 due to severe manpower issues, liquidity issues, and control weaknesses revealed in test of transactions [AR p.78].
benchmark_points.bp8: Internal audit was not adequate for the Company's size and operations [AR p.78, p.75].
benchmark_points.bp9: The CEO declares the adequacy and effectiveness of the Company's internal controls for financial reporting [AR p.62], which conflicts directly with the statutory auditor's conclusion [AR p.78].
benchmark_points.bp10: For the consolidated accounts, the auditor identified material weaknesses, including period-end reporting processes that were inadequate leading to errors in consolidation [AR p.150].
benchmark_points.bp11: The consolidated ICFR opinion is modified [AR p.146].
benchmark_points.bp12: Management states the Company has delayed some filings, but has since regularized them and necessary internal controls have been strengthened [AR p.28, p.31].
benchmark_points.bp13: The auditor states the Company is defaulting on its statutory and regulatory obligations [AR p.68] and is not regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues [AR p.73].
benchmark_points.bp14: The secretarial auditor reports ROC e-form delays through FY 2025-26 [AR p.37, p.63].
benchmark_points.bp15: Management states a Company Secretary vacancy from 16 June to 5 December 2025 caused MGT-14 delays of 36 days and 52 days [AR p.28].
benchmark_points.bp16: The secretarial audit table shows two MGT-14s: one due 02/09/2025 filed 24/10/2025 (52 days late) and one due 19/10/2025 filed 25/10/2025 (6 days late) [AR p.39].
benchmark_points.bp17: The second MGT-14 delay figure is 6 days, not 36 days as stated, and the excerpts do not explain the difference.
benchmark_points.bp18: The Company inadvertently missed a disclosure regarding the Maternity Benefit Act in the Directors' Report / Accounts, which is confirmed by the secretarial auditor [AR p.28, p.38].
benchmark_points.bp19: The Board claims it periodically reviews compliance reports and takes steps to rectify instances of non-compliances [AR p.51].
benchmark_points.bp20: The Company failed to finalise FY 2024-25 audited results on time, which were approved on 2 August 2025 and flagged by the PCS under Regulation 33 [AR p.31, p.38].
benchmark_points.bp21: Management states the Company has complied with the mandatory requirements of Regulation 27 [AR p.59], and the compliance table marks the Disqualification of Director check as Yes [AR p.29-30, p.41].
benchmark_points.bp22: The compliance table records that the Company defaulted on NCD repayments for over a year and that four directors are disqualified under Section 164(2)(b), creating an internal inconsistency with the Yes answer [AR p.41].
benchmark_points.bp23: The Board claims it is duly constituted with no change in composition [AR p.38] and independent directors have declared their independence [AR p.53].
benchmark_points.bp24: The PCS certificate names four directors as disqualified under Section 164(2)(b): Kashi Nath Chatterjee, Lily Bhushan, Mahendra Ujamshi Shah and Vishwas Madhusudan Joglekar [AR p.41, p.63, p.65].
benchmark_points.bp25: The statutory auditor states that based on written representations, all the directors are disqualified except two [AR p.70], which does not match the PCS statement.
benchmark_points.bp26: Kashi Nath Chatterjee and Mahendra Shah are on the Audit Committee [AR p.54].
benchmark_points.bp27: Management states the Company has complied with the directives of SAT [AR p.28, p.38, p.63].
benchmark_points.bp28: The PCS notes that the Company has complied with all compliances on the BSE Portal till date but is in the process of completing compliances with NSE [AR p.63].
benchmark_points.bp29: The Company states it emailed NSE during portal unavailability [AR p.43].
benchmark_points.bp30: Management states there are no RPTs requiring AOC-2 disclosure, no omnibus approvals, and no pecuniary relationships with directors or KMP beyond remuneration [AR p.33, p.52].
benchmark_points.bp31: The statutory auditor states that director remuneration paid was subject to a No Objection Certificate to be received from the consortium of lenders, and in the absence of NOC, it was not in accordance with Section 197 [AR p.70].
benchmark_points.bp32: The statutory auditor also reports that all related-party transactions are compliant in so far as their examination is concerned [AR p.75].
benchmark_points.bp33: The Board meets at least quarterly, decisions are unanimous, and systems exist to monitor compliance [AR p.51, p.38], which is confirmed by the PCS [AR p.38].
benchmark_points.bp34: The PCS's general opinion is limited because it did not verify the correctness of financial records and relied on the statutory auditor's report [AR p.39].
benchmark_points.bp35: The Board composition and procedures are corroborated by the secretarial auditor [AR p.38].
benchmark_points.bp36: The PCS reports no SEBI or stock exchange actions against the Company, and no penalties under Regulation 33 for the previous three years [AR p.41-42, AR p.59].
benchmark_points.bp37: Board Secretarial Standards, policies, website, and preservation of documents are reported as compliant [AR p.29-30, AR p.40-42].
benchmark_points.bp38: Audit trail (edit log) is enabled in the Tally system for stated periods with certain gaps [AR p.71, p.147].
benchmark_points.bp39: Current liabilities exceed current assets by ₹12,701.41 crore, and the auditor flags material uncertainty while the lenders' resolution plan has seen no progress [AR p.68].
benchmark_points.bp40: ₹391.76 crore of penal and incremental charges levied by lenders have not been debited to profit and loss and are disclosed as contingent liabilities [AR p.67].
benchmark_points.bp41: Tally's application-level edit log is retained only from 22 April 2024, and for the later Tally Prime version, it is only available from 20 November 2025 [AR p.71, p.147].
benchmark_points.bp42: Some subsidiaries' software has no audit trail at all [AR p.147].
benchmark_points.bp43: No liquid assets of ₹43.25 crore were set aside for the Debenture Redemption Reserve as required due to the financial crunch [AR p.86].
benchmark_points.bp44: Internal audit is not commensurate with the size and nature of the business [AR p.75, p.78].
benchmark_points.bp45: The excerpts do not include the full Board's explanations to each auditor qualification, the full Annexures, or the internal audit reports.
benchmark_points.bp46: The secretarial auditor expresses no view on financial records [AR p.39].
benchmark_points.bp47: The PCS's governance certificate is neither an assurance as to future viability nor of the efficiency or effectiveness of management [AR p.63].
benchmark_points.bp48: The excerpt at AR p.43 contains an unfilled placeholder (December [Year]), making the portal-restoration date unclear.
benchmark_points.bp49: The excerpts contain several unreconciled figures, such as the 36-day MGT-14 delay and the disqualification count.
benchmark_points.bp50: Reliance on the directors' statements about compliance, oversight and internal controls should be low because auditors contradict them on internal controls, CEO assurance, director eligibility, and filing compliance.

agent_points.ap1: In the holding company, all directors except two are disqualified as of March 31, 2026, under Section 164(2) of the Companies Act.
agent_points.ap2: The Company has defaulted in the repayment of amounts due to Non-Convertible Debenture (NCD) holders for a continuous period exceeding one year.
agent_points.ap3: The CEO declared that the Board of Directors and Senior Management affirmed compliance with the Code of Conduct for FY 2025-26.
agent_points.ap4: The CEO certified the accuracy of financial statements, the adequacy and effectiveness of internal controls for financial reporting, and compliance with SEBI Regulation 17(8).
agent_points.ap5: The Board defended its retention of ₹10.00 crore in contract claims as of March 31, 2026, relying on independent techno-legal consultants and arbitration experts.

agent_points.ap1: Inox Wind Limited (IWL) is entangled with the INOXGFL promoter group and its subsidiaries through multi-year supply orders, inter-corporate funding accommodations, shared corporate guarantees, and integrated business operations under a 'ONE INTEGRATED' strategy.
agent_points.ap2: Group entities like Inox Clean Energy Limited (ICEL) account for approximately one-third of Inox Wind's annual execution targets, backed by a 1.5 GW multi-year MOU.
agent_points.ap3: Subsidiaries like Inox Green Energy Services (IGESL) and Inox Renewable Solutions (IRSL) handle essential O&M and EPC services.
agent_points.ap4: The high degree of structural and operational entanglement introduces contagion and counterparty concentration risks for a lender, wherein cash flows, treasury operations, and project execution are heavily dependent on intra-group health.
agent_points.ap5: Risks are mitigated by formal related-party transaction limits, statutory disclosures, and the absence of non-performing asset (NPA) or willful defaulter classifications among key operating subsidiaries.
agent_points.ap6: As of March 31, 2026, the Promoter and Promoter Group hold a 44.18% stake, representing 76,35,13,104 voting rights or 44% of total voting rights in Inox Wind Limited.
agent_points.ap7: IWL is part of the INOXGFL Group, which possesses a market capitalization of US$ 16 billion and operates across diverse sectors including Refrigerants, Fluoropolymers, Speciality Chemicals, and Wind Energy & Renewables.
agent_points.ap8: The INOXGFL renewables business operates under a 'ONE INTEGRATED' strategy, creating an internal virtuous cycle of inter-play among group entities to provide multi-year revenue visibility.
agent_points.ap9: Inox Clean Energy Limited (ICEL), a group company operating in the renewable IPP and solar manufacturing space, has a targeted capacity addition of 14 GW by FY29.
agent_points.ap10: Approximately one-third of Inox Wind's annual execution targets for the coming years are expected to come from ICEL.
agent_points.ap11: Inox Wind signed a multi-year Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with ICEL for the supply of 1.5 GW of wind turbines.
agent_points.ap12: As of July 2026, Inox Wind maintains a comfortable order book size of ~4.4 GW.
agent_points.ap13: Because of large internal demand from ICEL, management notes it will be selective in taking new external orders.
agent_points.ap14: To meet customer requirements, facilitate integrated business arrangements, support project execution, and optimize working capital, treasury, and funding arrangements, IWL and its subsidiaries regularly undertake transactions with various Group entities.
agent_points.ap15: Inox Wind may avail financial assistance from its group entity Inox Clean Energy Limited and Promoter Director Shri Devansh Jain to meet fund requirements if the need arises.
agent_points.ap16: Transaction limits submitted for approval are designed to accommodate anticipated increases in project execution, supply volumes, corresponding working capital, treasury requirements, and potential inter-corporate funding and credit support.
agent_points.ap17: Inox Green Energy Services Limited (IGESL) is a 51.13% owned subsidiary providing O&M services.
agent_points.ap18: Inox Renewable Solutions Limited (IRSL) is an 88.83% owned subsidiary providing EPC services.
agent_points.ap19: Agreements involving guarantees, sureties, indemnities, or comfort letters between group entities may provide for indemnity rights, reimbursement obligations, counter-indemnities, and security arrangements.
agent_points.ap20: Neither IGESL nor IRSL has had their account classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) by any banker.
agent_points.ap21: Neither IGESL nor IRSL has been declared a willful defaulter by any bank or financial institution.
agent_points.ap22: Neither IGESL nor IRSL is undergoing insolvency resolution or liquidation, nor suffers disqualifications under Section 29A of the IBC, 2016.

per_question.query: How entangled is Inox Wind with its promoter group and subsidiaries - through orders, funding, guarantees and settlements - and what does that mean for a lender to Inox Wind itself?
